Perform only the Chrome-runtime smoke test. This unattended task explicitly requires the existing
Chrome extension and Default profile because the production run will play Loopit games there. Use
the `control-chrome` skill and select the `extension` backend; do not select `iab`.

The user has already authorized this scheduled workflow to open a new Chrome window. If the
Chrome backend is unavailable after setup, read the required bootstrap and Chrome troubleshooting
documentation, run `/usr/bin/open -a "/Applications/Google Chrome.app" --args
--profile-directory=Default about:blank`, wait briefly, and retry the `extension` backend once in
the same session. Do not ask for permission. The absolute app path is required because the runner's
LaunchAgent environment cannot resolve Chrome by display name.

The preceding workflow step already verified Codex,
GitHub, Uchuu Linear, Node, ffmpeg, Wrangler, tests, build, and deployment packaging. Do not
re-check those prerequisites or inspect the repository. Do not run shell commands except to read
the required browser skill/troubleshooting text and perform the single authorized Chrome recovery
command above when necessary.

Use Chrome through its connected browser backend, not standalone Playwright. Open a temporary tab
at `about:blank`, verify that its URL is exactly `about:blank`,
then close that tab. Do not modify files, create tickets, commit, push, upload media, deploy, or
print credentials. On success, respond exactly `BROWSER_PREFLIGHT_OK`. On failure, respond with
one line beginning `BROWSER_PREFLIGHT_FAILED:` and the factual reason.
